relations.subject: eventing:eventing-storage
relations.evidence: It should be noted, "document metadata" is different from the "Eventing Storage" keyspace (metadata collection), described in the next section, used by the Eventing Service to maintain state and checkpoints.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: What an Eventing Function sees is the actual event of the change, and hence it does not directly correlate with Database Triggers.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (shouldNotBeConfusedWith) - softer disclaimer than the trigger comparison ('Not exactly' rather than 'does not directly correlate')
relations.evidence:
Are Functions similar to a Rules Engine?  
Not exactly. A Rules Engine enforces ordering and other semantics that is not possible out of the box with Functions.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: Stored Procedures enforce a request-response model. A stored procedure will not be invoked automatically; it has to be invoked by a calling method. Functions are based on the idea of events.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: The Functions offering is about server-side processing or compute of business logic; it does not require any additional infrastructure layer or middleware to be deployed or managed. Couchbase's Kafka connector is an SDK component that needs an application container or middleware to run.

relations.subject: eventing:timer
relations.evidence: Yes. As of the release 6.6.0 Eventing Timers can be cancelled using _cancelTimer()_ function, or by creating a new Timer with the same reference as an existing Timer.

relations.subject: eventing:timer

relations.evidence: Yes. As of the release 6.6.0 Recurring Timers are fully supported, i.e. a function that is invoked by a Timer callback can reliably create fresh Timers.

notable_absence.finding: Despite being the longest page in this batch, the FAQ names no Capella role or privilege anywhere - all of its many questions are architectural/behavioral (DCP dedup, recursion, statelessness, node sizing, worker counts, encryption), not access-control questions. Confirms eventing-rbac.md (this batch) is genuinely the sole authoritative source for Eventing's access-control story; nothing here contradicts or supplements it.

cross_component_finding: This page restates, in different words, facts already captured with better evidence elsewhere in this batch: recursive mutation/recursion checks (eventing-Terminologies.json, troubleshooting-best-practices.json), the Eventing Storage keyspace's three-document-per-timer structure and space budgeting (eventing-timers.json), and the deploy/undeploy/pause/resume mutual exclusion with rebalance (eventing-lifecycle.json). No contradictions were found across any of these restatements - a good sign of internal consistency in Eventing's own documentation set.
cross_product_finding: The Functions-vs-Kafka-Connector comparison is a genuine, named cross-product reference within Couchbase's own portfolio (the Kafka Connector is a real, separate SDK-adjacent component), distinct from the crc64/Sync Gateway coupling found in eventing-language-constructs.json - Eventing's docs compare themselves against at least two other real Couchbase integration surfaces (Sync Gateway and the Kafka Connector), not just against generic outside concepts (triggers/rules engines/stored procedures).
